subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should internal OpenClaw agent turns add a strict tool-call enforcement policy for clear tool-required requests, and should that policy be default behavior or opt-in per agent/model?
rationale: Current source intentionally has mixed behavior across warning-only diagnostics, bounded compatibility promotion, and Gateway-only `tool_choice` enforcement, so changing the internal default is both a security and local-model compatibility decision.

options.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
options.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract for explicitly tool-required turns while preserving current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

options.title: Make strict enforcement default
options.body: Treat clear tool-required text-only turns as failures across internal agent runs, accepting upgrade and local-model compatibility risk as a security default change.

options.title: Fold into broader response gates
options.body: Defer this item to the larger pre-response gate and ledger-verification direction, trading a cleaner policy model for a larger design effort.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in strict enforcement
recommendation.body: Add a bounded strict mode or policy contract for explicitly tool-required turns while preserving current compatibility behavior by default until maintainers approve a default change.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is an agent-core security/default policy choice, and steipete authored recent adjacent agent-core dispatch-boundary work.
